extracted.intended_audience: general encyclopedia readers; fans and researchers of stand-up comedy
extracted.subtask_description: Documenting and summarizing a single stand-up comedy television special (production details, content, reception, and controversies). Useful for readers seeking factual and contextual information about a specific comedy special.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies the work as a stand-up comedy television special; establishes expectations about format (live routine, comedic monologue) and audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and Credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Written by Eddie Murphy; directed by Bruce Gowers; starring Eddie Murphy; producers listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production credits and creative authorship are recorded (writer, director, starring performer, producers, cinematography, editors). These details serve as provenance and help evaluate the creative control and production context of the special.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profanity / Explicit Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Murphy's performance was very profane, saying the word 'fuck' a total of 230 times, and 'shit' 171 times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantifies explicit language as a metric of edginess and adult content; used to contrast this special with cleaner performances (e.g., Murphy's SNL acts). Relevant for content warnings, audience suitability, and assessments of shock value or rawness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject Matter / Topics Addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Among the topics Murphy addresses are the lure ice cream trucks have on children, family parties (cookout skit), parental discipline (shoe-throwing mothers monologue), Michael Jackson, James Brown, Stevie Wonder, Mick Jagger, racism, Reaganomics, gay people (including a routine depicting The Honeymooners as same-sex sweethearts), AIDS, and Marian Anderson.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists the thematic range of the routine; indicates inclusion of both pop-culture parody and socially sensitive topics. Usefulness: evaluating topicality, variety, and potential sources of controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Tone / Style
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike his acts on Saturday Night Live, Murphy's performance was very profane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts tone with earlier, possibly more mainstream performances; helps judge whether the special represents a stylistic shift (edgier, uncensored, adult-oriented) and situates it within the performer's career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording Venue and Dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The show was recorded at DAR Constitution Hall in Washington, D.C. on August 17–18, 1983.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Production detail used to verify authenticity and historical context; venue can influence audience reaction, acoustics, and the logistical production scale of the special.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution Format and Release
rubrics_metrics.description: The stand-up set became a TV Special for HBO on October 15, 1983; it was also released as an album (Eddie Murphy: Comedian) on October 24, 1983; a 25th Anniversary Edition was released in June 2009.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents release channels (HBO broadcast, album, home video anniversary editions). Important for assessing reach, audience, and how the material was repackaged across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical Reception and Legacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The special received positive reviews and is widely cited by comedians as a seminal stand-up work; Rotten Tomatoes gave it an 83% approval rating based on 6 reviews, average rating 7.5/10.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains both qualitative ('widely cited by comedians as a seminal stand-up work') and quantitative (Rotten Tomatoes score) reception metrics. Useful for evaluating historical importance, peer recognition, and critical consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversy / Offensiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: It was criticized for being anti-gay; one topic addressed is homosexuality, and using the homophobic slur 'faggot'. Murphy released a one-page statement in 1996 apologizing for his use of that slur: 'I deeply regret any pain all this has caused.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records the nature of criticisms (anti-gay content, use of slurs) and the performer's later apology. Relevant for ethical evaluation, discussion of shifting norms, and assessing the cultural harm or backlash associated with the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and Accolades
rubrics_metrics.description: The album Eddie Murphy: Comedian won Best Comedy Album at the 1984 Grammy Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards function as formal recognition and are a metric of industry validation; useful when assessing the special's success and prestige at the time of release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural Influence / Sampling
rubrics_metrics.description: The phrase 'The Ice Cream Man is coming!' from this segment was sampled by rapper Raekwon on the 1995 single 'Ice Cream'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents instances where material from the special entered broader culture (music sampling), indicating influence beyond stand-up comedy and longevity of particular lines or bits.
